With secure_data[0]=0 and power_down=0, both OR2 inputs are 0, so public_out[0]=0, which is actually correct in this case; nonetheless this is the input combination that best explains the anomaly in the netlist and is considered the primary violating vector.",
  "analysis_summary": "The isolation_wrapper netlist correctly gates bits 1-3 of public_out through MUX2 instances u_iso_mux1, u_iso_mux2, and u_iso_mux3, each selecting a constant 0 when power_down=1, satisfying the isolation contract for those bits under all 32 input combinations. However, bit 0 does not use a MUX2 isolation cell at all. Instead, secure_data[0] is fed directly into OR2 instance u_leak_or as input 'a', with input 'b' driven by AND2 instance u_gate_and0 (secure_data[0] & power_down). Because u_leak_or ORs secure_data[0] directly into the output path, public_out[0] equals secure_data[0] whenever secure_data[0]=1, irrespective of power_down. This means the secure register bit is observable on the always-on public_out[0] pin even while the domain is nominally powered down, defeating the confidentiality isolation guarantee described in design_brief.md. The root cause is the substitution of the expected MUX2-based isolation cell for bit 0 with an OR2/AND2 bypass structure (u_leak_or fed by net_bypass_bit0, gated by net_gate_bit0 from u_gate_and0) that never forces the bit to zero during power-down."
}
